gloss: two steps; (shogi) the illegal move of placing two pawns on the same file

definitions.gloss: two steps; two paces (a literal pair of footsteps)
definitions.explanation: Two steps measured by walking. {歩|ほ} is the counter for steps in walking, so {二歩|にほ} = "two steps." Used both literally (two paces forward, back, or sideways) and metaphorically as a small distance or unit of progress.

definitions.gloss: (shogi) nifu — the illegal move of placing two unpromoted pawns on the same file
definitions.explanation: In shogi (Japanese chess), {二歩|にほ} is the foul of dropping a pawn ({歩|ふ}) onto a file (column) that already contains one of your unpromoted pawns. It is an immediate-loss rule violation, and is one of the most common and most embarrassing illegal moves a player can make.

examples.japanese: {二歩|にほ}⟦{歩|ある}いて→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦{止|と}まった→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧。
examples.english: I took two steps and stopped.
He stepped two paces forward and bowed deeply.

examples.japanese: ⟦{将棋|しょうぎ}→将棋：04172_shougi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{二歩|にほ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}って→打つ：01221_utsu⟧しまい、⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{負|ま}けて→負ける：01134_makeru⟧しまった。
examples.english: I dropped a pawn onto a file that already had one of my pawns and lost the shogi game on the spot.

examples.japanese: ⟦プロ→プロ：03871_puro⟧⟦{棋士|きし}→棋士：27809_kishi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{二歩|にほ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{反則|はんそく}{負|ま}け→反則負け：22305_hansokumake⟧になった⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{話題|わだい}→話題：03793_wadai⟧になった。
examples.english: A game in which a professional shogi player lost by foul because of nifu became big news.

examples.japanese: ⟦{将棋|しょうぎ}→将棋：04172_shougi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}えた→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{初心者|しょしんしゃ}→初心者：10149_shoshinsha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦うっかり→うっかり：01863_ukkari⟧{二歩|にほ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}って→打つ：01221_utsu⟧しまうこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Beginners who have just learned shogi often accidentally play nifu.

notes:
{二歩|にほ} has two distinct uses. The everyday meaning is the literal counter expression "two steps" (⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧ "two" + the counter ⟦{歩|ほ}→〜歩：00108_ho⟧ "step"). The specialized meaning, very familiar to anyone interested in Japanese chess, is the shogi rule violation of placing two unpromoted pawns on the same file.

COUNTER NOTES (Sense 1):
The counter ⟦{歩|ほ}→〜歩：00108_ho⟧ ("step") inflects irregularly:
- ⟦{一歩|いっぽ}→一歩：08890_ippo⟧: one step (note the doubling)
- {二歩|にほ}: two steps
- {三歩|さんぽ}: three steps
- {四歩|よんほ}: four steps
- {五歩|ごほ}: five steps
- {六歩|ろっぽ}: six steps (note the doubling)
- {七歩|ななほ}: seven steps
- {八歩|はっぽ}: eight steps (note the doubling)
- {九歩|きゅうほ}: nine steps
- {十歩|じゅっぽ}: ten steps (note the doubling)
- ⟦{何歩|なんぽ}→何歩：27348_nanpo⟧: how many steps

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (Sense 1):
- {二歩|にほ}⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: to step forward two paces
- {二歩|にほ}⟦{下|さ}がる→下がる：01188_sagaru⟧: to step back two paces
- {二歩|にほ}⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧: to walk two steps

SHOGI USAGE (Sense 2):
- {二歩|にほ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to commit a nifu (literally "to play [drop] a nifu")
- {二歩|にほ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{反則|はんそく}{負|ま}け→反則負け：22305_hansokumake⟧: to lose by foul because of nifu
- {二歩|にほ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{反則|はんそく}→反則：06541_hansoku⟧: the nifu foul / rule violation

The {歩|ふ}/⟦{歩|ほ}→〜歩：00108_ho⟧ kanji is read ふ when it refers to the shogi pawn piece itself, and ほ when used as a counter for footsteps. Despite the different on-the-spot reading, the two senses share the same kanji because the shogi name comes from the same character.

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- ⟦{一歩|いっぽ}→一歩：08890_ippo⟧: one step
- {三歩|さんぽ}: three steps
- ⟦{何歩|なんぽ}→何歩：27348_nanpo⟧: how many steps
- {歩|ふ}: pawn (the shogi piece)
- ⟦{将棋|しょうぎ}→将棋：04172_shougi⟧: shogi (Japanese chess)
- ⟦{反則|はんそく}→反則：06541_hansoku⟧: foul / rule violation

USAGE:
- The shogi sense of {二歩|にほ} is well known even to non-players in Japan, since it is one of the few well-known rules of the game and frequently appears in news headlines when a professional commits one.
- Outside the shogi context, the literal "two steps" meaning is the dominant one. Context normally makes the intended sense obvious.
